The exchange publishes the Bhav Copy after the session closes and we did not capture it live, so every row is published with unknown latency. available_utc is the session's close instant from mcx_sessions (evening close 23:30 or 23:55 IST per the hours circular in force, the 17:00 morning close on morning-only days, the Muhurat or budget-session close where one applies); for a session whose evening close no retained circular states, the later published close (23:55 IST) is used so the instant is never earlier than the true close.

Each row's state and stated hours come from the circulars in evidence_ids, and available_utc is 00:00 UTC of the day after the latest of their issue dates: the annual trading-holiday circular alone for the dates it governs, plus the Revision in Trading Hours circular that states the evening close where one covers the date, plus any single-date circular such as an election closure, a Muhurat timing or a budget-day live session. Every row is published, so a default point-in-time read returns it from its available_utc on. The open and evening-only dates from 2026-11-02 to 2026-12-31 are published from the 2026 holiday circular alone, available from 2025-12-16, because no retained Revision in Trading Hours circular covers them. Their evening close is 23:55 with hours_notified false: the later of the two closes MCX has used since October 2020, a bound that is never earlier than the real close and not a time any circular states. A row is not revised once a release has carried it: an hours circular issued later applies only to dates added after 2026-12-31.

A session row is available at the settlement publication of the session: that session's close instant from mcx_sessions, the same convention mcx_daily uses. The exchange publishes at or after the close and we did not capture at that instant, so the class is published. The row holds only what is known at that instant: the session's designation, bars, high, low and settlement. It carries nothing derived from the legs of swings.parquet, which are known only once confirmed.

A swing row is available from confirm_available_utc: the settlement publication of the session of the bar that completed the leg, that session's close instant from mcx_sessions, the same convention mcx_daily uses. A leg is only a swing once the price has reversed threshold_pct from its extreme, and that reversal can print sessions after the extreme, so no row is knowable earlier. The exchange publishes at or after the close and we did not capture at that instant, so the class is published. available_utc, the settlement publication of the session the extreme printed in, is a data column and not the availability of the row. The bar instants are not availability: an hourly bar carries the quotes' own clocks (mcx_quotes states exact or published per row) and a daily bar carries the session's opening instant, inside which the Bhav Copy high and low printed at an unknown time, and confirm_utc is a bar instant of that kind.
